**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 08:56
- [USER] User requested a summary of a specific section of text.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The section allows the Secretary, in consultation with the Director of National Intelligence, to designate any foreign government or regime as a foreign adversary if they find that the government or regime is engaged in a long-term pattern or serious instances of conduct significantly adverse to the national security of the United States or security and safety of US persons.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The designation can be removed if the Secretary determines that the government or regime is no longer engaging in such conduct.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Secretary must notify certain congressional leaders and committees 15 days before making or removing a designation.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] The assistant provided a summary of the section, capturing the key points regarding the designation and removal of foreign adversaries, as well as the notification requirement to Congress.
